passages.english: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone— for kings and all those in authority—so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.

lines.text: First of all, then, Paul urges us to pray to God.
Offer petitions to God for everyone — bring people's needs to Him.
Offer prayers to God for everyone.
Offer intercessions to God for everyone — plead with Him on behalf of others.
And offer thanksgiving to God for everyone — give Him thanks for them.
Pray for kings.
And pray for all those in authority.
We pray so that we may live peaceful lives.
And we pray so that we may live quiet lives.
Then we can live in complete godliness.
And we can live with dignity.

passages.english: This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

lines.text: Praying for everyone is good.
And praying for everyone pleases God.
God is our Savior.
And God wants everyone to be saved.
So God wants everyone to come to know the truth.

passages.english: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all—the testimony that was given at just the right time.

lines.text: There is one God.
And there is one mediator between God and people — a mediator is someone who brings two sides together.
This mediator is the man Christ Jesus.
Jesus gave Himself as a ransom for everyone — a ransom is the price paid to set a captive free.
And this is the testimony — Christ dying for us sinners proves God loves us.
This testimony was given at just the right time — Christ didn't die too early or too late in history, but at just the right time.

passages.english: For this reason I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a faithful and true teacher of the Gentiles. I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything.

lines.text: For this reason God appointed Paul.
God made Paul a preacher and an apostle — Christ sent Paul out with His authority.
And God made Paul a teacher of the Gentiles — the Gentiles are all the nations who are not Jews.
Paul taught the Gentiles faithfully.
And Paul is a true teacher of the Gentiles.
Paul is telling the truth.
Paul is not lying about anything.

passages.english: Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension.

lines.text: Therefore Paul wants the men everywhere to pray.
Paul wants men to lift up holy hands when they pray.
Holy hands are hands not stained by sin.
Paul wants men to be without anger.
And Paul wants men to not argue.

passages.english: Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with respectable apparel, with modesty, and with self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes, but with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God.

lines.text: Paul also writes to the women.
Paul wants women to dress themselves in respectable clothing — for example, nothing sexual or revealing that would tempt someone to lust.
Paul wants women to dress with modesty — modesty meant not dressing to show off.
And Paul wants women to dress with self-control.
Paul does not want women to dress with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes — in Paul's day these were how a rich woman showed off her wealth.
Instead of clothing, Paul wants women to make themselves beautiful with good deeds.
Beauty from good works is proper for women who say they worship God.

passages.english: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.

lines.text: Paul does not permit a woman to teach — in verse 11 Paul said what a woman must do while learning, and here Paul says what she must not do.
Paul does not permit a woman to exercise authority over a man — to exercise authority over someone is to be in charge of him, so that he must do what you say.
A woman must not teach a man in a way that puts her in charge of him — Paul puts teaching and authority together in one sentence, so teaching that takes charge is not permitted.
Instead, a woman is to remain quiet — this is the same quietness as in verse 11, which is being settled and ready to receive, not having no words at all.
Instead, a woman is to remain quiet — Paul began verse 11 with quietness and ends verse 12 with quietness, so quietness is what both verses are about.

passages.english: A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.

lines.text: A woman must learn — in Paul's day women were often not taught, so Paul commands that women be taught.
A woman must learn in quietness — quietly listening to receive right teaching, not interrupting or taking over the teaching herself.
A woman must learn in quietness — if she talks on and on, she is implying the man rightly teaching should listen in quietness, and then she would be the one teaching him.
And a woman must learn in full submissiveness — to be submissive is to yield to the man rightly teaching her.
